questions.explanation:
LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`def countdown(limit):` — Creates reusable behavior; without the definition, callers cannot invoke or share this rule.
`for value in range(limit, 0, -1):` — Processes each iterable item; without the loop, remaining items are skipped.
`yield value` — This line continues the calculation or control flow; omitting it removes that step and may change later results.
`print(list(countdown(3)))` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.

questions.prompt: Which statement accurately describes “Iterators and generators”?
options: A dictionary maps an ID to a profile or a product name to a price; `get` handles a missing key safely.
Lists hold ordered results, carts, or task queues; remember that indexing starts at zero.
Iterators and generators process large streams without loading everything into memory; exhausted generators must be recreated.
Tuples hold fixed groups such as coordinates, while sets hold unique labels; choose based on ordering and duplicates.
questions.answer: Iterators and generators process large streams without loading everything into memory; exhausted generators must be recreated.
